identity.title: AGN Torus Detectability at Submillimeter Wavelengths: What to Expect from ALMA Continuum Data

paper_type_evidence.quote: We study the detectability of the emission associated with the AGN dusty structure at sub-mm wavelengths using ALMA, in a theoretical and observational way.
ALMA continuum flux densities have been collected analyzing the products continuum Stokes I maps available for each projects at the ALMA archive web page

question.value: Can the dusty AGN torus be detected at sub-mm wavelengths with ALMA continuum data, given contamination by synchrotron jet emission?

evidence.quote: It is the aim of this paper to study the detectability of extended emission associated to AGN dusty structure at sub-mm wavelengths using ALMA.

analysis_steps.goal: Predict torus flux ratio at sub-mm

method.value: Scale 12um flux from X-ray via Asmus15 relation; use Nenkova08B clumpy SEDs for F_sub-mm/F_12um, linear extrapolation beyond 1000 um

evidence.quote: We linearly extrapolate the SEDs above 1000$\rm{\mu m}$ to estimate the expected flux at 3000$\rm{\mu m}$ (i.e. band 3 at 100 GHz).

analysis_steps.goal: Predict jet flux ratio at sub-mm

method.value: Extrapolate Bonchi13 fundamental plane to 100, 353, 666 GHz with alpha in [-0.5,-0.7], L_X 1e42-1e46, MBH 1e6-1e9

findings_qualitative.value: NGC 1052 sub-mm emission is jet dominated; for other sources neither torus nor jet explains the sub-mm flux; I Zw1 is the most promising torus candidate but unresolvable

evidence.quote: The radio jet of NGC 1052 dominates over the torus in the sub-mm range. In all the other cases, neither the torus or the jet can explain the sub-mm emission.

claims.hypothesis: Which tori are detectable at sub-mm with ALMA
claims.experiment: Scaling-relation + clumpy model predictions vs ALMA rms
claims.result: Highest torus contribution at 666 GHz; 1 mJy torus detectable in 1h at 353 GHz or 10h at 666 GHz
claims.finding: Only bright, large, dense tori are detectable, with possible jet contamination

evidence.quote: We find that it is more likely to detect bigger and denser dusty tori at the highest ALMA frequency (666 GHz/450 $\mu$m).

claims.hypothesis: Observed sub-mm fluxes of four AGN are explained by torus plus jet
claims.experiment: Combine mid-IR smooth-model and radio fits and extrapolate
claims.result: Only NGC 1052 explained (jet); others under-predicted by factors ~3, 8, 100
claims.finding: I Zw1 is the best torus candidate; SED analysis with radio data is needed

evidence.quote: neither the torus or the jet can explain solely or as combined effect the sub-mm emission with a ratio between data and model of $\rm{\sim}$3, 8 and even 100 for NGC 1068, NGC 3516, and I Zw1

why_this_method.value: Smooth Fritz06 model chosen as simplest baseline not needing a stellar component

evidence.quote: is the simplest baseline model that satisfactory describes the data

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Five dusty models tested; others need extra stellar component

evidence.quote: For the others, a stellar component[^9] is needed to account for the short wavelengths (below 10$\rm{\mu m}$).

limitations_admitted.value: Fundamental plane is a rough jet estimator; large ALMA beams may overestimate fluxes

evidence.quote: the fundamental plane is a rough estimator of the sub-mm contribution of the jet
